answers.brief_reasoning: Loop: add n%10 to sum, then n/=10, until n is 0. If n is 0 the loop never runs, so it returns 0.

Start at start and add 1 until n % digitSum(n) == 0. For n >= 1 the digit sum is at least 1, so we never divide by zero. Every number from 1 to 9 is Harshad, and Harshad numbers come often enough that the loop ends.
